display.purpose: The hero headline on the public home page, set in white over the Commission Green scrim. One per page, and only where a photograph backs it.

headline.purpose: Section headings on public pages and the page title in staff applications.

title.purpose: Card titles, including notice titles in the public feed. Line-height 1.0 keeps the title tight against its date line.

body.purpose: All reading text, including Tiptap-rendered notice bodies. Measure capped at 65-75ch.

label.purpose: Buttons, form labels, table cells, badges, metadata. The workhorse size across all four staff applications.

overline.purpose: Uppercase, letterspaced. The agency's name in the public footer and the footer's column headings. Structural only.

shadows.name: hairline
shadows.purpose: Vestigial edge on inputs and outline buttons. Do not extend to new components.

shadows.name: resting-card
shadows.purpose: The single step cards take. Borders do the real separating.

shadows.name: floating-layer
shadows.purpose: Popovers, dropdown menus, dialogs, sheets, and toasts - elements that genuinely leave the page plane.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Default for hover, focus, and color/box-shadow state changes on buttons, inputs, and badges.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The primary action on any screen. One per view; Commission Green marks the agency's action, not decoration.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 8px 16px; border: none; border-radius: 8px; background: var(--primary, oklch(0.5364 0.1457 150.5842)); color: var(--primary-foreground, oklch(0.9556 0.0199 112.9333)); font-family: Roboto, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.25; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: all 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, oklch(0.5364 0.1457 150.5842)) 90%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring, oklch(0.5353 0.1357 153.5529)) 50%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; pointer-events: none; }

components.name: Lifecycle Button
components.description: A state transition performed as a deliberate act - Publish, Archive, Cancel, Close, Resolve. Never a switch or checkbox (ADR 0001). Relabels to 'Save and Publish' when the form beneath it is dirty.

components.name: Text Input
components.description: The standard field across all staff forms and the public request intake. Always paired with a real label; the placeholder never substitutes for one.

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: A record's state, always spelled as a word. Published and Pending take the filled green; Archived takes pale green; Draft takes the outline variant. The pill radius is reserved for this component alone.
components.html: Published Archived Draft

components.name: Notice Card
components.description: The public notice feed's unit. A bordered surface a half-step above paper, with a ruled header carrying the title and publication date, a fade-clipped excerpt, and a ruled footer for the notice type.

narrative.overview:
This is an archival register that happens to be a website. The Commission's authority does not come from persuasion - it comes from the fact that what is posted here *is* the legal notice, and that nothing posted is ever quietly lost. Cancelled meetings stay visible. Archived notices stay reachable. The visual system exists to make that permanence feel deliberate rather than accidental: hairline rules, generous dates, columnar order, and a green so specific to this agency that it needs no explanation.

The surfaces are warm, not clinical. Every neutral in the light theme carries a faint green cast (hue 150), so backgrounds read as paper in daylight rather than as a gray dashboard. Structure is carried entirely by borders and tonal steps, never by shadow. The result should feel crisp and institutional - tight registration, consistent rhythm, a faint formality - without ever tipping into decoration. A resident who arrives asking whether their street is being sprayed should get the answer and forget the interface existed.

Two failure modes are rejected by name. The first is startup SaaS: gradient meshes, glassmorphism, oversized marketing heroes, "Get Started Free." This is a New Jersey county agency, not a product launch. The second is municipal-site decay: clip-art seals, unstyled link lists, tables from 2006, PDFs used as the interface. Being civic is not a license to be ugly. The system lives in the narrow band between them, and both edges are equally out of bounds.
keyCharacteristics: Green-cast neutrals throughout - warm paper, not cold gray
Flat by default; borders and tonal steps carry all structure
One type family, Roboto, working across five applications
Status is always spelled as a word, never encoded in color alone
Uppercase and letterspacing are structural, never decorative
One design system, five frontends: packages/ui is the only visual authority

rules.name: The One Green Rule
rules.body: Commission Green is the only color on a resting screen that carries meaning by itself. Reserve it for the agency's mark, the primary action, and the active navigation state. It is never a background for decoration, never a highlight, and never used twice in the same visual group.

rules.name: The Status Is A Word Rule
rules.body: A record's state - Draft, Published, Pending, Archived, Cancelled, Closed, Resolved, New - is always spelled out in the badge. Color may reinforce it; color may never be the only thing carrying it. This is a WCAG requirement on the public site and a legibility requirement everywhere else.

rules.name: The Hue-150 Rule
rules.body: Every neutral in the light theme sits on hue 150 at low chroma. A neutral pulled from outside that family will read as a foreign gray against the rest of the page, however close its lightness.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Roboto sets everything. There is no display face, no serif for long reading, and no accent family. A second family is a system change, not a page decision.

rules.name: The Uppercase Is Structural Rule
rules.body: Uppercase with 0.025em tracking marks the agency's identity block and column headings in the footer. It never appears on a button, never on a heading a visitor reads for content, and never as emphasis inside a sentence.

rules.name: The Eighty-Rem Rule
rules.body: No content region exceeds max-w-7xl (80rem). The hero photograph may bleed past it; nothing readable may.

rules.name: The Shell Owns The Chrome Rule
rules.body: Staff applications import mcmec-layout and fill it. An app that defines its own sidebar, header, or breadcrumb has forked the system, and four forks is how five applications stop looking like one.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A shadow means the element is genuinely above the page and can be dismissed. Cards, tables, inputs, buttons, and panels are held by their border and their tonal step. If a new component wants a shadow to feel separated, it needs a border instead.

rules.name: The Pill Is A Status Rule
rules.body: A fully rounded shape means "this is the state of a record." Nothing else in the system - no button, no tag, no avatar frame, no input - is a pill.

rules.name: The Lifecycle Is A Button Rule
rules.body: State transitions are performed, not set. If a design shows a record's state as a toggle, a select, or a checkbox, the design is wrong regardless of how it looks - see docs/adr/0001-lifecycle-actions-are-buttons.md.

dos: Do keep every neutral on hue 150 at low chroma so surfaces read as one warm material.
Do let borders in Rule (oklch(0.8 0.02 150)) carry structure. Reach for a border before a shadow, every time.
Do spell out record state as a word inside the badge, with color as reinforcement only.
Do compose staff screens from mcmec-layout and packages/ui. A pattern solved once is solved for all five frontends and every one added later.
Do use the CONTEXT.md vocabulary in visible copy - "Spray Mission," "Public Request," "Notice" - regardless of what a legacy route path says.
Do cap reading measure at 65-75ch on the public site and keep max-w-7xl as the outer bound everywhere.
Do preserve the 3px focus ring at 50% opacity on every interactive element. It is the only focus treatment in the system.
Do keep uppercase and letterspacing structural - the footer identity block and column headings, nothing else.
donts: Don't add a second type family. Roboto sets everything until the system says otherwise.
Don't consume --font-serif or --font-mono while Lora and Fira Code remain unloaded.
Don't put a shadow on a resting surface. Cards, tables, panels, and inputs are flat.
Don't use Commission Green decoratively. It marks the agency, the primary action, and the active state - nothing else.
Don't let the chart-1 to chart-5 pastels out of the Weekly Mosquito Activity chart. They are a species series, not a UI palette.
Don't use a pill radius for anything that isn't a status badge.
Don't render a lifecycle action as a switch, checkbox, or status dropdown.
Don't hide a disabled action. Show it disabled so staff can see the action exists.

Don't bury, paginate, collapse, or lazily defer a statutorily required posting - a legal Notice within its seven-day Retention Period, a meeting agenda, or a cancelled meeting. Layout may never obstruct the public record.
Don't reach for gradient meshes, glassmorphism, or marketing-hero patterns. Equally, don't accept clip-art seals, unstyled link lists, or PDFs standing in for an interface.
